title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Brunei: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Brunei: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Brunei: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: When a citizen of Brunei Darussalam dies in Brunei, statutory deadlines for reporting and registration are unusually tight, and estate administration follows a dual-court system separating Syariah Faraid orders for Muslims from civil probate grants for non-Muslims. Completing medical or coroner clearance, civil registration, and National Retirement Scheme (SPK) notifications in sequence prevents penalties and bank delays. This checklist summarizes official obligations under Brunei legislation and judiciary, immigration, and retirement portals [1][2][4][6].

steps.title: Immediate medical certification and Coroner clearance
steps.html:
• Hospital or attended death: The attending medical practitioner issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form F) and hospital discharge documents needed by civil registrars and burial or cremation authorities [1][2].
  • Home, sudden, or unexplained death: Report the death immediately to the Royal Brunei Police Force and the Magistrates' Court Coroner Office under the Coroners Act (Chapter 63A); a Magistrate serving as Coroner conducts inquiries by designated district zoning before releasing the body and issuing a Coroner's certificate [9].
  • Verify personal particulars early: Confirm the deceased's full name, Brunei Identity Card (Smart IC) number, and exact date and cause of death across hospital and police records before attending civil registration [2][10].

steps.title: Rapid civil registration and obtaining death certificates
steps.html:
• Strict statutory deadline under Cap. 79: Under the Births and Deaths Registration Act (Chapter 79) administered by Immigration and National Registration Department (INRD), ordinary death reporting carries a strict initial timeframe of 12 hours of death (with late recording up to 3 days and post-registration rules thereafter under Sections 13 and 14) [1][2][11].
  • Documents required for registration: Present Form F or the Coroner's certificate, the deceased's original Identity Card, and the informant's identity card at the Births, Deaths and Adoptions Division of Immigration and National Registration Department (INRD), which issues the official Death Certificate (Sijil Kematian) [2][3][10].
  • Order certified extracts: Request certified copies of the Death Certificate immediately for probate courts, banks, pension funds, and overseas institutions [2][10].

steps.title: Burial, cremation, repatriation, and Hague Apostille authentication
steps.html:
• Burial and cremation coordination: Religious burial arrangements for Muslims proceed swiftly through local mosque and religious authorities once medical or police clearance and registration documents are obtained, while non-Muslim burials and cremations follow municipal and cemetery permit controls [1][2].
  • International transport of remains: Repatriating remains or ashes abroad requires the Brunei Death Certificate, embalming or cremation certificate, non-infectious disease medical clearance, passport cancellation, and airline customs permits [10].
  • Hague Apostille in force since 1987: Brunei Darussalam is a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (in force 3 December 1987); Supreme Court of Brunei Darussalam (Chief Registrar, Deputy Chief Registrar, and Registrars, alongside Subordinate Court Magistrates and Registrars) serves as the Competent Authority under Article 6 and issues Apostilles at a BND 2.00 fee per certificate [8].

steps.title: SPK / TAP retirement funds, survivorship, and identity returns
steps.html:
• Notify Tabung Amanah Pekerja (TAP): Inform Tabung Amanah Pekerja (TAP) promptly of the death via the e-Amanah portal or customer counter so SPK (Skim Persaraan Kebangsaan, which replaced legacy TAP and SCP accounts) savings withdrawals and Survivorship Protection / Derivative Benefits for eligible surviving spouses, children under 21, or parents can be processed [6][7].
  • Administrator Nominee vs. un-nominated accounts: Where the deceased registered an Administrator Nominee on e-Amanah, TAP disburses funds to that nominee to distribute lawfully under Faraid or a valid will; without a registered nominee, claimants must first submit an Administration Appointment Letter from the Probate Office [4][6].
  • Surrender government documents and notify banks: Return the deceased's Brunei Smart Identity Card to INRD, surrender the passport for cancellation, and notify local banks and utility accounts with the official Death Certificate [2][10].

steps.title: Dual-system probate, Syariah Faraid, and resealing
steps.html:
• High Court Probate Office jurisdiction: Under the Probate and Administration Act (Chapter 11) and Wills Act (Chapter 193), Probate Office of the High Court (Judiciary of Brunei Darussalam) issues Grants of Probate (with a valid will), Letters of Administration (on intestacy), Summary Administration for intestate estates not exceeding BND 25,000, and Resealing of foreign Commonwealth grants [4][5].
  • Mandatory Faraid Certificate for Muslim estates: As confirmed by Probate Office of the High Court (Judiciary of Brunei Darussalam) and the Islamic Family Law Act (Chapter 217), estates of Muslim decedents require a Syariah Court Faraid Order both when there is a will (limiting Wasiat dispositions under Islamic law) and on intestacy before civil probate administration completes distribution [4][12].
  • Property, tax, and foreign powers: Brunei levies no personal income tax or estate inheritance tax on individuals, though land transfers and share registrations require formal probate or Faraid orders; any instrument from overseas requiring local registration must follow notarization and Apostille certification, and Attorney General's Chambers (AGC) Brunei Darussalam maintains public legislation and registry oversight [4][5][8][13].

contacts.name: Immigration and National Registration Department (INRD)
contacts.note: Processes birth and death registrations, issues official Death Certificates, and handles identity card surrender under Cap. 79.

contacts.name: Probate Office of the High Court (Judiciary of Brunei Darussalam)
contacts.note: Issues Grants of Probate, Letters of Administration, Summary Administration for estates up to BND 25,000, and grant resealing.

contacts.name: Tabung Amanah Pekerja (TAP)
contacts.note: Administers National Retirement Scheme (SPK) Next-of-Kin Withdrawals, Administrator Nominee claims, and Derivative Benefits via e-Amanah.

contacts.name: Supreme Court of Brunei Darussalam
contacts.note: Designated Article 6 Competent Authority under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (BND 2.00 per Apostille).

contacts.name: Attorney General's Chambers (AGC) Brunei Darussalam
contacts.note: Publishes Laws of Brunei Darussalam and operates statutory registries including Powers of Attorney.
